snapshots.name: Raskolnikov
snapshots.subtitle: A destitute former student in St. Petersburg
snapshots.body: Living in a cramped, rented garret and behind on rent he cannot pay, he has withdrawn from friends and studies alike to brood over an idea he cannot quite bring himself to name. He sets out one hot evening on what he calls, to himself, only a rehearsal.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Sonia
snapshots.subtitle: Marmeladov's daughter, forced into prostitution
snapshots.body: Gentle and devout despite the life circumstances have forced on her, she supports her stepmother and half-siblings with money earned on the street. Raskolnikov hears her story from her drunken father before he ever meets her.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Razumihin
snapshots.subtitle: Raskolnikov's loyal former fellow student
snapshots.body: Poor himself but relentlessly cheerful and resourceful, he has kept up his friendship with Raskolnikov even as the latter has cut off nearly everyone else. He takes it on himself to look after his friend once Raskolnikov falls seriously ill.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Porfiry
snapshots.subtitle: The examining magistrate investigating the murders
snapshots.body: A relation of Razumikhin's, sharp, talkative, and fond of drawn-out psychological sparring rather than direct accusation. His conversations with Raskolnikov circle the case with unsettling patience.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Dounia
snapshots.subtitle: Raskolnikov's younger sister
snapshots.body: Intelligent, proud, and recently freed from an ugly situation as a governess, she has just become engaged to a lawyer she does not love in order to help her brother. She and their mother travel to St. Petersburg expecting a joyful reunion.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Pulcheria Alexandrovna
snapshots.subtitle: Raskolnikov's mother
snapshots.body: Devoted and anxious about her son, whose infrequent, evasive letters have started to worry her badly. She travels to the capital with Dunya, hoping to see her son settled and well.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Luzhin
snapshots.subtitle: Dunya's wealthy, self-satisfied fiancé
snapshots.body: A middle-aged lawyer of some means who has proposed to Dunya expecting a wife grateful enough to defer to him in everything. Raskolnikov takes an instant dislike to him, sight unseen, from his sister's letter alone.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Svidrigaïlov
snapshots.subtitle: Dunya's former employer, with a dark reputation
snapshots.body: Wealthy, unsettling, and recently widowed, he pursued Dunya while she worked in his household and is rumored to be responsible for terrible things. His arrival in St. Petersburg alarms the whole Raskolnikov family.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Marmeladov
snapshots.subtitle: Sonya's father, a ruined former civil servant
snapshots.body: A hopeless drunkard who has driven his family into poverty and his daughter onto the street, he pours out his shame to Raskolnikov in a tavern with startling, self-lacerating honesty. His account is the reader's introduction to Sonya before she ever appears.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Katerina Ivanovna
snapshots.subtitle: Marmeladov's consumptive second wife
snapshots.body: Once a genteel officer's daughter, now reduced to poverty and illness, she is proud, quick-tempered, and fiercely protective of her children by her first marriage. Her situation only worsens after her husband's accident.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Alyona Ivanovna
snapshots.subtitle: An elderly pawnbroker
snapshots.body: Miserly and widely disliked, she lends small sums against pledged goods at punishing rates from her cramped apartment. Raskolnikov has visited her before to pawn a watch and a ring.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Lizaveta
snapshots.subtitle: Alyona Ivanovna's simple, put-upon half-sister
snapshots.body: Meek and constantly at her sister's beck and call, she trades goods and does errands around the neighborhood, where Sonya and others know her as harmless and kind. She happens to keep company with the pawnbroker at an unfortunate hour.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Lebeziatnikov
snapshots.subtitle: Luzhin's roommate, a follower of fashionable new ideas
snapshots.body: Earnest and easily excitable about the latest progressive theories, he shares lodgings with Luzhin and disapproves of his roommate's treatment of Sonya. His convictions are more sincere than his judgment.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Nastasya
snapshots.subtitle: The landlady's servant who looks in on Raskolnikov
snapshots.body: Blunt but not unkind, she brings Raskolnikov what food and news he gets in his isolated garret room. She is often the only person he speaks to for days at a stretch.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Zossimov
snapshots.subtitle: A young doctor, Razumikhin's friend
snapshots.body: Called in to attend Raskolnikov during his illness, he takes a professional, faintly curious interest in his patient's strange symptoms. He and Razumikhin discuss the case with more frankness than Raskolnikov would like.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Ilya Petrovitch
snapshots.subtitle: A police lieutenant nicknamed Gunpowder
snapshots.body: Excitable and quick-tempered at the district police station, where Raskolnikov is summoned on an unrelated debt matter not long after the murders. His temperament earns him a nickname among the clerks.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Zametov
snapshots.subtitle: A police clerk
snapshots.body: Young and sharp, he is present at the station when Raskolnikov faints during questioning about the debt, and later listens, startled, as Raskolnikov half-jokingly describes exactly how he might have committed the murders. Razumikhin introduces the two over drinks.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Mikolka
snapshots.subtitle: A house painter who confesses to the murders
snapshots.body: Working in the building at the time of the crime, he unexpectedly comes forward and confesses to a crime he did not commit, complicating the investigation considerably. Porfiry does not seem nearly as convinced by the confession as the reader might expect.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Polenka
snapshots.subtitle: Katerina Ivanovna's eldest daughter
snapshots.body: Still a child, she is old enough to help look after her younger siblings and to feel her family's poverty and shame keenly. Raskolnikov shows her an unexpected tenderness.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.
